A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: In a Moscow cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage (IA-IIIA) NSCLC, those who quit after diagnosis had an adjusted hazard ratio for all-cause mortality of 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85); this is observational and does not measure the effect of offering cessation help at the first visit.
supported_en: Annals of Internal Medicine (2021): quitting after diagnosis was linked to HR 0.67 (0.53–0.85) for death from any cause in 517 smokers with early-stage NSCLC.
not_supported_en: I found no evidence on how many patients actually quit when cessation help is offered at the first visit, so the full 0.67 applies only to those who quit.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found of a standing order giving cessation medication and counselling at the first specialist visit, either at Lapha or at OYS; the OYS pathway page only says that help with medication is available.
summary_en: I found no public sign that Lapland or OYS runs this measure. OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says that stopping smoking improves outlook even after diagnosis and that medication can help, but it describes no routine where every smoker gets medication and counselling at the first visit; Lapha's digital pathway for surgery patients, started in October 2026, covers only back, knee and hip surgery. A study published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2021 found 33% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.67) in early-stage lung cancer patients who quit after diagnosis, but the study only observed patients and did not test this kind of first-visit routine.
unanswered_en: Two more searches found no Lapha page on a cessation nurse service or a written cessation routine for lung cancer patients.
